lessons.title: Forage Species Selection
lessons.body: Choosing the right forage for your sheep depends on your climate, soil, and how you plan to graze. In Africa, you need plants that survive dry seasons and produce enough protein. For wet, high-rainfall areas like the Kenyan highlands, plant Rhodes grass (Chloris gayana) or Napier grass (Pennisetum purpureum). Rhodes grass yields 10-15 tonnes of dry matter per hectare per year and tolerates heavy grazing. Napier grass gives up to 30 tonnes but needs good rainfall and fertilizer. For drier zones, use buffel grass (Cenchrus ciliaris) or Bermuda grass (Cynodon dactylon). Buffel grass survives on 300 mm annual rainfall. Add legumes like lucerne (alfalfa), desmodium, or stylo (Stylosanthes) to boost protein. Lucerne has 18-22% crude protein and fixes nitrogen, reducing fertilizer costs. Desmodium works in humid areas and is shade-tolerant. Stylo thrives in poor, acidic soils. For a small farm, mix one grass and one legume. Example: Rhodes grass + desmodium. Sow grass at 10-15 kg per hectare and legume at 2-4 kg per hectare. In dry areas, plant at the start of the rains. Test germination before sowing: put 100 seeds in a wet cloth for 7 days and count how many sprout. If less than 70 sprout, buy new seed. Avoid toxic plants like bracken fern or Crotalaria species, which can poison sheep. Rotate species every 3-4 years to prevent pest buildup. Always buy certified seed from a registered agrodealer to avoid weeds and low yields.

lessons.title: Rotational Grazing Systems
lessons.body: Rotational grazing means moving sheep between paddocks to let grass recover. Without it, sheep overgraze and eat the best plants first, leaving weeds. A simple system for 20 sheep: divide your pasture into 4-6 paddocks using electric fencing or live fences like sisal or thorny hedges. Each paddock should be 0.5 to 1 hectare. Move sheep every 3-5 days in the rainy season and every 7-10 days in the dry season. The key rule: graze half, leave half. When grass is 15-20 cm tall, let sheep in. When they eat it down to 5-7 cm, move them. This gives plants enough leaf area to regrow. Rest each paddock for 30-45 days in the wet season and 60-90 days in the dry season. In dry periods, you may need to reduce flock size or buy supplementary hay. A practical tool is a grazing chart: draw your paddocks and mark the date you move sheep. Use a notebook or a simple phone app like Pasture Map. For 20 sheep, you need about 0.4 hectares per month of rest. So if you have 2 hectares, you can keep 20 sheep with 5 paddocks. In East Africa, many farmers use a 'cell grazing' system with daily moves using portable electric netting. This improves grass yield by 30-50% and reduces worm burden because sheep don't graze where they pooped 3 days ago. Always provide clean water and mineral licks in each paddock. Rotational grazing saves money on feed and vet bills.

lessons.title: Soil Fertility and Testing
lessons.body: Healthy soil grows healthy grass. You need to know your soil's pH, nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K). In Africa, most soils are acidic (pH below 5.5) and low in P. Get a soil test from a local agricultural office or a private lab. In Kenya, KALRO does tests for about 1,000 KES per sample. Take samples from 10 spots in your pasture, mix them in a bucket, and send 500g to the lab. If you can't afford a lab, use a simple soil test kit from an agrodealer. For pH, you can also use vinegar: if soil fizzes, it's alkaline (pH above 7); if it doesn't, it's likely acidic. For acidic soil, apply agricultural lime at 2-4 tonnes per hectare. Lime raises pH and releases nutrients. Do this 2-3 months before planting. For nitrogen, plant legumes like desmodium or lucerne. They fix 50-200 kg of N per hectare per year. For phosphorus, apply triple superphosphate (TSP) at 100-200 kg per hectare at planting. For potassium, wood ash or muriate of potash (MOP) at 50-100 kg per hectare works. Manure is excellent: apply 5-10 tonnes of well-rotted cattle or goat manure per hectare per year. Spread it in the dry season and incorporate it lightly. Avoid fresh manure; it burns plants and spreads weeds. Test your soil every 2-3 years. Keep records of what you apply and when. If grass turns yellow, it needs nitrogen. If it's purple, it needs phosphorus. If leaf edges burn, it needs potassium. Fix deficiencies early to avoid poor grazing.

lessons.title: Weed and Pest Control
lessons.body: Weeds compete with grass for water and nutrients. The worst weeds in African pastures are thorny plants like Lantana camara, blackjack (Bidens pilosa), and couch grass. For small farms, hand-pull weeds before they flower. For larger areas, use a slasher or mower to cut weeds before they seed. Mulching with dry grass or straw suppresses weeds and keeps soil moist. For chemical control, use glyphosate (Roundup) carefully. Spray only on a calm day and avoid grazing for 7 days. For thorny bushes, cut them at the base and paint the stump with a herbicide like triclopyr. Always wear gloves, boots, and a mask. Pests include termites, armyworms, and locusts. Termites eat grass roots. Control them by destroying mounds and applying neem cake (200 kg per hectare) or a registered insecticide like imidacloprid. Armyworms appear in the rainy season. Scout your pasture weekly. If you see 5-10 caterpillars per square meter, spray with Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) or neem oil. Locusts are harder: report outbreaks to your local agriculture office. They may spray. For sheep, internal parasites like worms are a pest. Rotational grazing reduces worm larvae. Also, use copper sulfate foot baths for foot rot. Keep a weed and pest diary. Record what you see, when, and what you did. This helps you act faster next season. Never use a herbicide on a windy day or near water sources. Always store chemicals away from children and animals.

lessons.title: Irrigation and Water Management
lessons.body: Sheep need clean water daily: 4-10 litres per adult per day, more in hot weather. But your pasture also needs water. In dry seasons, irrigation keeps grass growing. For small farms, use a treadle pump or a solar-powered pump. A 1-horsepower solar pump can irrigate 0.5 hectares. Drip irrigation is best: it saves 30-50% water compared to sprinklers. Lay drip lines 30 cm apart along grass rows. For a 1-hectare pasture, you need about 20,000-30,000 litres per week in dry weather. Water early morning or late evening to reduce evaporation. Mulch around plants with dry grass to hold moisture. Build a small dam or water pan to catch rainwater. Line it with clay or a plastic liner to prevent seepage. A 10m x 10m x 2m pan holds 200,000 litres, enough for 2 hectares for a month. For sheep drinking water, use troughs with a float valve to keep them full. Clean troughs weekly to prevent algae and mosquitoes. In dry areas, harvest rainwater from roofs into tanks. A 5,000-litre tank costs about 30,000 KES and can water 20 sheep for 3 months. Test water quality: if it's salty or has a bad smell, send a sample to a lab. Sheep can tolerate up to 5,000 ppm total dissolved salts, but young lambs need cleaner water. Always provide shade near water points. In very dry periods, reduce stocking rate. You can also feed hay and silage instead of relying on irrigated pasture.

lessons.title: Hay and Silage Making
lessons.body: Hay and silage let you feed sheep when grass is scarce. Hay is dried grass; silage is fermented wet grass. To make hay, cut grass when it's tall and before it seeds. In the morning, cut with a sickle or mower. Let it dry in the sun for 2-3 days, turning it daily. Test dryness: twist a handful; if it breaks, it's ready. If it's still flexible, dry more. Bale it with a manual baler or store loose in a dry shed. Good hay is green, smells sweet, and has 8-12% moisture. Store on pallets to avoid dampness. For silage, cut grass when it's wet and wilt it for 4-6 hours. Chop into 2-3 cm pieces. Pack tightly into a pit, drum, or silo bag. Add molasses (2-3% of weight) to help fermentation. Seal with plastic and soil. It ferments in 3-4 weeks. Good silage smells like vinegar and is yellow-green. Feed 1-2 kg per sheep per day. A 200-litre drum holds about 150 kg of silage. For 20 sheep, you need 2-3 tonnes of hay or silage for a 3-month dry season. Make hay in the rainy season when grass is abundant. In Kenya, many farmers make hay from Rhodes grass or oats. In West Africa, use maize stover or groundnut haulms. Always store in a dry, ventilated place. Never feed mouldy hay or silage; it causes disease. Test by smelling: if it's musty or black, throw it away. With good hay and silage, you can keep your sheep healthy all year.

quiz.q: Which forage grass is best for a dry area with 300 mm annual rainfall?
quiz.explanation: Buffel grass is drought-tolerant and survives on 300 mm rainfall.

quiz.q: What is the recommended sowing rate for grass seed per hectare?
quiz.explanation: Grass seed is typically sown at 10-15 kg per hectare for good coverage.

quiz.q: Which legume is shade-tolerant and suits humid areas?
quiz.explanation: Desmodium grows well in humid, shaded conditions.

quiz.q: How many seeds out of 100 should germinate for good seed quality?
quiz.explanation: At least 70% germination is needed; below that, buy new seed.

quiz.q: Which plant is toxic to sheep?
quiz.explanation: Crotalaria species contain alkaloids that can poison sheep.

quiz.q: In rotational grazing, when should you move sheep to a new paddock?
options: A) When grass is 5 cm tall
B) When grass is eaten down to 5-7 cm
D) When grass is 30 cm tall
quiz.explanation: Move sheep when grass is grazed to 5-7 cm to allow recovery.

quiz.q: How many paddocks are recommended for a simple rotational system?
quiz.explanation: 4-6 paddocks allow adequate rest periods for grass regrowth.

quiz.q: What is the rest period for a paddock in the wet season?
quiz.explanation: In wet seasons, grass recovers in 30-45 days.

quiz.q: How much land is needed per month of rest for 20 sheep?
quiz.explanation: About 0.4 hectares per month of rest supports 20 sheep.

quiz.q: What is a benefit of rotational grazing?
quiz.explanation: Rotational grazing reduces worm larvae by avoiding grazing where sheep recently defecated.

quiz.q: What is the ideal soil pH for most pasture grasses?
quiz.explanation: Most grasses grow best at pH 5.5-6.5.

quiz.q: Which nutrient deficiency causes yellowing of grass?
quiz.explanation: Nitrogen deficiency leads to yellowing (chlorosis).

quiz.q: How much agricultural lime is recommended for acidic soil?
quiz.explanation: 2-4 tonnes per hectare raises pH effectively.

quiz.q: Which fertilizer is a good source of phosphorus?
quiz.explanation: Triple superphosphate is high in phosphorus.

quiz.q: How often should you test soil?
quiz.explanation: Testing every 2-3 years is sufficient for most pastures.

quiz.q: What is a sign of potassium deficiency in grass?
quiz.explanation: Potassium deficiency causes leaf edge burn.

quiz.q: Which weed is thorny and problematic in African pastures?
quiz.explanation: Lantana camara is a thorny invasive weed.

quiz.q: How long should you wait before grazing after spraying glyphosate?
quiz.explanation: Wait 7 days to allow herbicide to break down.

quiz.q: Which pest eats grass roots?
quiz.explanation: Termites damage grass by eating roots.

quiz.q: What is a natural control for armyworms?
quiz.explanation: Bt is a biological pesticide effective against caterpillars.

quiz.q: How much water does an adult sheep need per day?
quiz.explanation: Adult sheep drink 4-10 litres daily, more in heat.

quiz.q: Which irrigation method saves the most water?
quiz.explanation: Drip irrigation reduces water use by 30-50%.

quiz.q: How much water does a 1-hectare pasture need per week in dry weather?
quiz.explanation: 20,000-30,000 litres per week is typical for 1 hectare.

quiz.q: What is the capacity of a 10m x 10m x 2m water pan?
quiz.explanation: Volume = 10 x 10 x 2 = 200 cubic meters = 200,000 litres.

quiz.q: Why should you clean water troughs weekly?
options: A) To prevent algae and mosquitoes
C) To make sheep drink more
quiz.explanation: Cleaning prevents algae growth and mosquito breeding.

quiz.q: What is the maximum total dissolved salts sheep can tolerate?
quiz.explanation: Sheep can tolerate up to 5,000 ppm TDS, but lambs need cleaner water.

quiz.q: When is the best time to cut grass for hay?
quiz.explanation: Cut before seeding for best quality and regrowth.

quiz.q: How do you test if hay is dry enough to bale?
quiz.explanation: Dry hay breaks when twisted; if flexible, it needs more drying.

quiz.q: What percentage of molasses is added to silage?
quiz.explanation: 2-3% molasses aids fermentation.

quiz.q: How long does silage take to ferment?
quiz.explanation: Silage ferments in 3-4 weeks when properly sealed.
